newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares up in heavy cement, mills trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares up in heavy cement, mills trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose slightly on Tuesday in trading dominated by cement and milling stocks, brokers said.
The Capital Markets Authority (CMA) overall index closed 0.1 points up at 235.03 points with an above-average turnover of 27.05 million pounds ($7.96 million).
"It was a busy day, investors still have a strong market sentiment," said Ahmed el-Helw, vice president at brokers Hermes Financial.
Cement giants continued to rally with Egyptian Tora Portland Cement dominating the day's activity. Shares worth 5.66 million pounds were traded but it closed unchanged at 57.00 pounds.
"This reflects real demand and supply for the firm," Helw said.

Suez Cement closed 0.25 pounds higher at 46.25 after shares worth 2.81 million pounds exchanged hands while Helwan Portland Cement closed unchanged at 44.00 after trade in shares worth 1.39 million pounds.

There was also heavy trade in milling shares, with North Cairo Flour Mills leading the way. The stock, which Helw calls the Cairo market's "sleeping beauty" closed 3.88 pounds higher at 99.00 after more than 36,000 shares were traded.
Southern Cairo Flour Mills also traded heavily, closing the day 0.25 pounds higher at 51.25.
Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN jumped 23.00 pounds to close at 820.00 on heavy demand.
"It's a good share, and its natural for investors to buy it," Helw said.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 349.22 points from 352.01 on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose slightly to 160.73 from 160.72.
